lessons.concept: An array is a contiguous sequence. A pointer identifies an object, not its length. Structures group fields; enums name states. Here a checked array interface passes register and bit values to a pure function.

Create an unsigned one-bit mask.

lessons.topics: PMSM/BLDC terminology; pole pairs; mechanical/electrical angle; six-switch inverter; R-L-back-EMF model; torque/load
lessons.opt: Start at zero load; use 0.005-0.02 N m only after stable no-load operation in simulation.
lessons.graph: Speed rises toward equilibrium; q-axis current rises with load. Excess load causes droop or stall.
lessons.rig: NUCLEO-G474RE + X-NUCLEO-IHM08M1 + compatible low-voltage three-phase PMSM/BLDC + 24 V supply. Initial work is simulation-only.

controls.low: No load leaves only viscous loss.
controls.nominal: 0.01 N m fits the model current capability.

controls.name: q-axis voltage
controls.high: More voltage increases speed and startup current.

lessons.concept: This surface-PMSM dq model uses R=2 ohm, Ld=Lq=2 mH, p=4, flux=0.01 Wb, J=0.0002 kg m^2 and B=0.0001 N m s/rad. They are consistent illustrative parameters, not the purchased motor.
lessons.contract: in: [id A, iq A, mechanical w rad/s, vd V, vq V, load N m]. out: [did/dt, diq/dt, dw/dt, torque N m].
algorithm: Compute electrical speed from pole pairs.
Evaluate coupled current derivatives.
Compute torque and mechanical acceleration.
lessons.limits: Average inverter; no switching ripple, thermal or saliency model. Forward Euler dt=10 us in the browser; simulation diverging beyond bounds is stopped, not clipped.

lessons.topics: shunt; amplifier gain; ADC reference; offset calibration; two/three-shunt reconstruction; centre-aligned PWM; trigger point
lessons.opt: Near the centre of a stable conduction window; avoid switching edges and amplifier settling interval.
lessons.graph: PWM edges create noise spikes; correctly placed samples lie on the flat current region.
lessons.rig: Motor stack powered at low current limit; scope may observe 3.3 V trigger/test point only. Do not attach a grounded hobby scope to U/V/W.

lessons.title: Clarke and Park transforms
lessons.outcome: Transform phase currents into stationary alpha-beta and rotating d-q quantities, then reconstruct them.
lessons.topics: balanced three-phase constraint; Clarke; electrical angle; Park; sign convention; inverse Park; power consistency
lessons.opt: Sweep full 0-360 degrees; for aligned current vector, iq or id should remain nearly constant by the declared convention.
lessons.graph: Three sinusoids become a rotating alpha-beta vector; Park makes it nearly stationary.
lessons.rig: Simulation first. Hardware current samples and encoder/Hall angle may later replace simulated values.

controls.name: Electrical phase
controls.high: 360 degrees returns to the same vector.

controls.name: Angle-estimate error
controls.low: Negative error leaks q into negative d.
controls.nominal: 0 gives id=0, iq=1 A for the supplied vector.
controls.high: Positive error leaks q into positive d.

lessons.concept: The amplitude-invariant Clarke transform assumes balanced phase currents. The Park sign convention is explicit. A pure q-axis current produces constant iq only when the estimated angle follows the true electrical angle.
lessons.contract: in: [ia A, ib A, electrical theta rad]. out: [alpha A, beta A, id A, iq A, inverse alpha, inverse beta].
algorithm: Apply Clarke with balanced-current assumption.
Rotate by the estimated electrical angle.
Invert Park and check reconstruction error.
lessons.limits: Radians in C; degrees only in UI. No sensorless angle estimation. A stationary angle is not an adequate replacement for rotor feedback.
lessons.mutation: Wrong Park sign breaks rotation and the inverse test.
lessons.coverage: Graded core: in: [ia A, ib A, electrical theta rad]. out: [alpha A, beta A, id A, iq A, inverse alpha, inverse beta]. Other topics listed are theory or extension work, not additional simulated hardware.

lessons.graph: Current follows reference. Saturation clips voltage; good anti-windup recovers quickly without long overshoot.

controls.nominal: 0.5 A is a model target, not a hardware limit.
controls.high: 3 A may require more voltage than available.

controls.nominal: 2 V sustains at most 1 A in a 2-ohm static RL load.

controls.name: Anti-windup
controls.low: 0 permits integrator windup in the reference comparison.

equations: integrate if unsaturated or error drives back toward range
lessons.concept: A PI controller cannot command unlimited voltage. For this isolated RL current-loop experiment R=2 ohm, L=2 mH, Kp=2 V/A and Ki=500 V/(A s). It is not the full dq loop; vector limiting is implemented in M5.
lessons.contract: in: [error A, integrator V, Kp, Ki, dt s, limit V, AW 0/1]. out: [applied voltage, next integrator, saturation flag].
algorithm: Calculate raw proportional-plus-integral output.
Saturate applied voltage.
Update the integrator only when allowed.
lessons.limits: Controller executed every 50 us. RL model substepped at 10 us. No switching, ADC delay or back EMF in this isolated experiment.
lessons.mutation: Unconditional integration winds up during saturation.
lessons.coverage: Graded core: in: [error A, integrator V, Kp, Ki, dt s, limit V, AW 0/1]. out: [applied voltage, next integrator, saturation flag]. Other topics listed are theory or extension work, not additional simulated hardware.

lessons.opt: 0.2-0.8 for clear linear operation; requests beyond the feasible span must be limited before duties are generated.
lessons.graph: Three duties shift together with common mode; line-to-line voltage remains correct. Overmodulation shows a warning.

controls.high: Above 1 triggers circular vector limiting.

controls.name: DC bus
controls.high: Never apply this range blindly to a motor.

lessons.concept: Limit the vector before computing duties. Common-mode shifts all phase commands equally, leaving their line-to-line differences unchanged. Three complementary inverter legs create six gate signals; common mode is not a fourth motor wire.
lessons.contract: in: [alpha V, beta V, Vdc>0]. out: [duty U,V,W, vector scale, limited alpha, limited beta].
algorithm: Validate positive bus voltage.
Scale alpha/beta together into the linear circle.
Calculate three phases, common mode and duties.
lessons.limits: Average modulation model; gate animation illustrates complementary logic with both-off dead time. Not a transistor-loss or shoot-through simulator.
lessons.mutation: Removing the vector limit can request infeasible duties.

lessons.opt: Start 100-300 rpm after alignment; ramp gradually. Included generic motor may not have Hall sensors, so sensored work needs a sensor-equipped motor or simulation.
lessons.graph: Reference ramps; actual speed follows with limited iq. Angle error or excessive load causes oscillation/fault.
lessons.rig: Motor stack plus compatible Hall/encoder-equipped motor for physical sensored FOC; otherwise simulation-only.

lessons.topics: two-rate simulation; numerical step; parameter variation; overcurrent/undervoltage/overspeed; deadline monitor; metrics; raw logs
lessons.opt: Use the selected motor/driver rated range; for current cart, 24 V nominal with conservative firmware current limit. Do not infer motor current from adapter rating.
lessons.graph: Speed/current/voltage/fault share a synchronized time axis; trips latch and PWM disables.

equations: fault priority: latch, sensor, UV, OV, |I|, |rpm|, deadline
fault != 0 => PWM disabled; re-arm only after reset and checks
lessons.concept: A digital twin is only as trustworthy as its equations, integration and comparison evidence. The reference combines the dq plant, two-rate loops, vector limiter and explicit fault events. Fault flags are recorded alongside waveforms.
lessons.contract: in: [Vbus V, phase-current A, rpm, sensor-valid 0/1, deadline-ok 0/1, prior fault code 0..6]. out: [fault code, PWM enabled]. Codes: 1 SENSOR,2 UV,3 OV,4 OC,5 OS,6 DEADLINE.
algorithm: Validate discrete flags.
Preserve the previous fault code.
Evaluate fault priority only if not latched.
Enable PWM only with code zero.
lessons.limits: Post-trip coast uses a passive mechanical approximation. It omits body-diode currents, regeneration and DC-bus dynamics; not suitable for hardware brake sizing.
